A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NSReg research and are readable throughout, including equations, figures and tables. The supplied v1 ends with references; v2 includes Appendices A–C. References to supplementary material in v1 do not establish content outside the supplied PDF.

before.justification: v1 reports original anomaly-detection experiments on Photo, Computers, CS and Yelp, including baseline comparisons, ablations, sensitivity studies and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds large-graph evaluations, further baselines and regulariser comparisons, representation visualisations and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: v2 introduces an adjustable weight lambda into the previously unweighted combination of detection and regularisation losses (Equations 2 and 6). It uses lambda=2 for ogbn-proteins and 1 otherwise. The three relation types, representation architecture and inference procedure remain substantively unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluations on ogbn-arxiv and ogbn-proteins while retaining all four original datasets. These extend coverage to substantially larger citation and protein graphs, including a biological network domain absent from v1.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds DOMINANT, GGAN, CoLA, TAM and AMNet to the six retained baselines. AMNet also enters data-efficiency and runtime comparisons. The ablation comparisons additionally evaluate supervised and unsupervised contrastive regularisers, expanding the alternatives tested against NSR.

E3.justification: The original main-text settings and AUC-ROC/AUC-PR metrics are retained. The added large-graph experiments use 100 labelled anomalies, 1% labelled normal nodes and 400 training epochs at learning rate 0.001. Appendix C.2 additionally evaluates the seen-anomaly subset. Newly disclosed preprocessing details do not establish changes to earlier experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds contrastive-regularisation controls, a normal–anomaly relation ablation, seen-only performance analysis, representation/score-contour case studies and sensitivity to lambda. The earlier hypersphere and two-relation ablations remain, with the latter renamed NSR (dual). Appendix C.5 also supplies AUC-ROC data-efficiency curves absent from the supplied v1.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five random runs and mean-plus-standard-deviation table reporting. However, the vertical error bars in v1's alpha-sensitivity Figure 3 are omitted from the corresponding v2 Figures 5–6. Changed average-column standard deviations do not, by themselves, establish a changed statistical procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for new baselines, large graphs, regularisers and appendix analyses. Original per-dataset means in Table 1 remain unchanged, but average-column standard deviations are revised. SAD ablation scores also change: Photo all-anomaly AUC-PR moves from 0.127 in v1 Table 3 to 0.269 in v2 Tables 3 and 7, without an explanation of the revision.

T1.justification: The open-set assumptions and relation-label definitions are retained, and neither version presents theoretical guarantees or proofs. v2's added GraphSAGE update equation explains the encoder already specified in v1 rather than introducing new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain normal-structure regularisation, reduced overfitting to seen anomalies, improved unseen-anomaly detection and integration into other supervised detectors. The rewritten abstract and introduction preserve these claims; the six-dataset statement describes expanded supporting evidence.

C2.justification: Appendix C.2 explicitly interprets lower seen-anomaly average AUC-PR than BCE (0.710 versus 0.743) as a fitting–generalisation trade-off. Sections 4.8 and C.3 add explanations involving gradient-scale compatibility and redundant normal–anomaly relations. These qualify and extend the retained normality-based explanation.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B newly provide training/evaluation pseudocode, dataset statistics, anomaly-class selection rules, Yelp graph-view and clustering details, weighted sampling, dependency versions, neighbour-sampling counts, scoring-network dimensions and baseline training settings. These substantially expand reproducibility information; they do not establish that previously reported implementations changed.

R1.justification: v2 expands citations within the existing related-work categories, including additional semi-supervised graph/fraud detectors, graph augmentation and imbalanced-learning work, plus references supporting new baselines and datasets. Its positioning around unseen-anomaly generalisation and its distinction from PReNet remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Parts of the abstract and introduction are rewritten, relation-prediction terminology becomes relation modelling, and authorship/header text changes. New appendix sections organise implementation details and additional results. The main section sequence and much of the existing exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially redraws the architecture diagram, adds representation visualisations, expands comparison tables and reorganises the earlier ablation tables into Tables 3 and 7. Data-efficiency and sensitivity displays are split or relocated across the main text and appendix. The document also adopts a different conference layout with author blocks and running headers.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the central mechanism through alternative regularisers, broader baseline comparisons, large-graph tests and an explicit seen-anomaly trade-off analysis. Appendix B supplies important dataset-construction and implementation information missing from the supplied v1. These gains outweigh reporting defects: Algorithm 2 misdefines the unseen set relative to the prose, Tables 3 and 7 swap contrastive-method labels, and sensitivity error bars disappear. Those defects still limit reproducibility and interpretability.
